prompt: Our team built a TradingAgents-style multi-agent LLM trading system on GPT-4o: four analyst agents, a bull/bear researcher debate, a trader agent, and an LLM risk manager that makes the final call. We backtested it on the current S&P 500 constituents from Jan 2023 to Dec 2024, trading at the close of the day each signal is generated, with no transaction costs. After trying about 40 prompt variants, the best one has an annualized Sharpe of about 2.2. returns.csv has the daily returns of that best variant and of an equal-weight buy-and-hold benchmark. My manager wants to present this to the investment committee next week. Is the result credible? Write review.md with your verdict, the specific problems, any numbers you compute from the data, and what we need to do before presenting.
assertions: Gives a clear verdict that the result is not credible / not presentable as-is
Flags survivorship bias from using current S&P 500 constituents
Flags GPT-4o pretraining look-ahead for 2023-2024 and recommends post-cutoff or anonymised evaluation
Flags selection from ~40 prompt variants and computes or applies a deflated Sharpe ratio or equivalent correction
Flags execution at the signal-day close and recommends next-open/next-bar execution
Flags missing transaction costs and recommends a cost model with sensitivity
Computes performance statistics from returns.csv (e.g. Sharpe, drawdown)
Uses a dependence-aware or paired method for uncertainty (block bootstrap, HAC/Newey-West, or paired test vs benchmark)
Compares the strategy against the benchmark (excess return, alpha/beta, or difference test)
Flags the LLM risk manager as the final decision node and recommends a deterministic risk gate after it (jailbreak/injection risk)
Recommends a sealed out-of-sample or walk-forward holdout for prompt selection
